---
title: "Customising"
---


The theme is split so that the common case — same structure, different
colours — touches one small file and nothing else.

## Where things live

```
_extensions/zotqda-theme/
├── _extension.yml       the format: theme pair, highlight pair, defaults
├── zotqda.scss          shared defaults and ALL rules
├── zotqda-light.scss    light palette — colours only
└── zotqda-dark.scss     dark palette — colours only
```

`zotqda.scss` carries every structural rule (header, grid, sidebars,
pills, callouts) written against SCSS variables with `!default`
values. The palette files override those variables and contribute no
rules. Order matters and is codified in `_extension.yml`: in Quarto's
theme lists, **later files win the defaults**, so the palettes come
after the shared file.

## Your own colours

Edit the palette files, or add your own pair next to them and point
`_extension.yml` at it. The variables a palette actually sets, with
the light values as they ship:

```scss
$zq-accent:     #3f51b5;   // indigo — active markers, links
$zq-accent-ink: #3547a8;   // slightly deeper, for links on white
$zq-ink:        #212630;   // body text
$zq-muted:      #5d6572;   // sidebars, footer
$zq-surface:    #f5f6f8;   // code blocks, banners
$zq-border:     #e5e7eb;
$zq-navbar-bg:  #ffffff;   // frosted header (80% opacity applied)
$zq-pill:       rgba(63, 81, 181, 0.10);  // the active-page pill
```

The palettes also map a handful of Quarto/Bootstrap variables
(`$body-bg`, `$link-color`, `$code-bg`, …) onto those. Everything else
falls back to the shared defaults in `zotqda.scss`.

## Your logo instead of the book

The open-book glyph before the site title is a placeholder, drawn as a
Bootstrap-icon glyph in CSS so that no image file is needed. To replace
it with a logo, use Quarto's own mechanism —

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    logo: assets/logo.svg
```

— and neutralise the glyph rule in a palette or a site-level SCSS:

```scss
.navbar-title::before { content: none; }
```

## Site-level additions

Anything page- or site-specific belongs in the site, not in the theme:
Quarto merges `css:` and `theme:` additions from `_quarto.yml` on top
of the format. The zotQDA sites add only `fonts/noto.css` this way.

One caution: the rules layer targets Quarto's HTML classes, and a few
rules carry `!important` or raised specificity because Quarto's own
rules would otherwise win. If an override of yours seems to do
nothing, look at those first — each is commented in `zotqda.scss`
where it happens.
